durability_caveats: APFS guarantees atomicity and ordering; it does NOT by itself provide append-only immutability against a writer who owns the containing directory. Nonreuse must be enforced by the owner application, not assumed from the filesystem.
No at-rest encryption (FileVault OFF) means journal confidentiality and tamper evidence depend entirely on the owner principal, not on a storage boundary.
The repo working tree is NOT a journal substrate: it is version-controlled, unsigned (commit.gpgsign not configured), has no active git hooks, and is rewritable by the same principal.

filesystem_facts.tmp_filesystem: apfs but volatile; unsuitable for durable custody

finding_2_journal_feasibility.question: Can a single-writer durable journal with atomic sequence and nonreuse capability exist at this chosen deployment?
finding_2_journal_feasibility.verdict_at_filesystem_grain: FEASIBLE. APFS provides exclusive create, atomic rename, advisory whole-file locking and durable file AND directory fsync. A single-writer durable journal with an atomic monotonic sequence and nonreuse guarantee is constructible on the Data volume.

what_governs_actual_physical_writer_iden.consequence: Physical writer identity is governed by exactly one human being. Any journal under that principal is, in custody terms, writer and verifier reachable by the same actor.
what_governs_actual_physical_writer_iden.governing_principal: ONE human principal (uid 501) who is simultaneously the console user, the admin-group member, and the current shell principal
what_governs_actual_physical_writer_iden.sudo_gate: password required, held by the same single human principal

finding_4_design_level_boundaries.bootstrap_collision_rollback_fork: UNDESIGNED. No bootstrap, collision, rollback or fork-boundary handling exists for a C1 AT07 build registry. These remain design-level questions, deliberately unallocated by this commission.
design_level_observations_for_the_future: Advisory locking plus exclusive create is sufficient for a single-writer design, but the owner application must additionally enforce sequence monotonicity and nonreuse, because APFS will not.
A journal inside the git working tree is unsuitable: unsigned, rewritable, and version-controlled rather than append-only.
Any fork or collision defence ultimately rests on the owner principal's exclusivity, which on this host is a single human being.
Rollback semantics must be defined so that a rolled-back sequence number can never be reissued; nothing currently prevents that.
finding_4_design_level_boundaries.epoch: NO epoch space exists. No epoch machinery appears anywhere in the C1/N10E/AT07 lane. The only epoch symbols in the tree are in V3 contact-witness lanes, which are out of scope here and forbidden. NO epoch number was allocated.
finding_4_design_level_boundaries.genesis: NOT CONCEIVED, NOT ALLOCATED, NOT WRITTEN
finding_4_design_level_boundaries.immutable_pinned_roots: NO pinned root exists. No trust_root or issuer_root symbol exists in any code surface. The single OWNER_ROOT constant found is a frozen GT34 literal and is NOT a root.
finding_4_design_level_boundaries.registry_or_registrar: NO REGISTRAR symbol exists in any code surface. There is no active registrar to consult.
finding_4_design_level_boundaries.sequence_monotonicity_nonreuse: NO nonreuse, non_reuse or C1-lane monotonicity guard exists. pre553_c11_repository.py does contain collision logic, but that belongs to the C11 repository lane, not the AT07 owner lane, and must not be borrowed as owner authority.
